title: Trains to Eastbourne
lead: These are the trains I would look at for Airbourne. Southern runs a train from London Victoria to Eastbourne every half an hour, through Clapham Junction, East Croydon and Gatwick, and the coast trains bring you in from Brighton and Hastings. I’ve added a few connections that work well too, like Thameslink from St Pancras with a quick change at East Croydon. Pick your station, a day and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
facts: Every day, all four show days
Every 30 minutes from London, hourly on Sundays
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for Airbourne. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: From the station it’s about 10 to 15 minutes on foot. Head down through the town centre to the seafront, then walk west along the prom to the Western Lawns by the Wish Tower. On show days there are plenty of stewards and signs, and you can just follow the crowd.
walkBack: Allow about 15 minutes to walk back up to the station from the Western Lawns, and a bit more when the crowds leave.
note: Due to how complicated the rail network is, this page only shows trains run by Southern, plus the Thameslink and Gatwick Express trains that connect with them. Times are from the National Rail timetable for Thursday 5 to Sunday 8 November 2026, checked on 30 October 2026. Times for summer 2027 usually come out in the spring, so please check with Southern before you travel. The line is drawn along the railway, so treat it as a guide. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
gaOnly: Southern trains, plus a few connections. Due to how complicated the rail network is, I only show Southern trains into Eastbourne, plus the Thameslink and Gatwick Express trains that connect well with them, as they’re all run by the same company. If you’re coming from further away, I would plan your trip to one of these stations first and pick it up from there.

x.hubSub: Southern’s main stations, and a few that connect. Pick the one you’re starting from, or heading home to.
x.arrTick: Southern trains into Eastbourne on a {day}. The London trains come in through Lewes and Polegate, and the coast trains run in from Brighton and Hastings.
x.liveArr: Live arrivals into Eastbourne from across the Southern network. It updates every minute.
x.lastTrain: In the current timetable the last train back to {hub} on a {day} leaves Eastbourne at {last}{chg}{gets}. On the Sunday evening there are usually fireworks on the seafront, so I would check this before you settle in for them.
x.extraTrains: Southern usually runs longer trains on show days, and the summer 2027 times come out nearer the show. Weekend engineering works on the Brighton line are common too, so please check before you travel.

about.London Victoria|Clapham Junction: Out over the Thames on Grosvenor Bridge, right by Battersea Power Station.
about.Clapham Junction|East Croydon: Through the south London suburbs, past Balham and Streatham Common.
about.London Bridge|East Croydon: Out past the Shard and through the south London suburbs, with Norwood Junction just before Croydon.
about.London St Pancras|East Croydon: Under the City through Farringdon, across the Thames at Blackfriars, then out through London Bridge and the south London suburbs.
about.East Croydon|Gatwick Airport: Over the North Downs and through the Merstham tunnels. Keep an eye out for aircraft as you come into Gatwick.
about.Gatwick Airport|Haywards Heath: Past Three Bridges and across the Ouse Valley Viaduct, just after Balcombe. It’s one of the finest bits of Victorian railway in the country, so it’s worth looking out of the window.
about.Three Bridges|Haywards Heath: Through Balcombe and across the Ouse Valley Viaduct, one of the finest bits of Victorian railway in the country.
about.Haywards Heath|Lewes: Off the main line just after Wivelsfield, then across the Sussex countryside under the South Downs.
about.Lewes|Polegate: Along the foot of the South Downs, past Glynde and Berwick.
about.Lewes|Eastbourne: Along the foot of the South Downs, past Glynde and Berwick, then through Polegate and Hampden Park into Eastbourne.
about.Polegate|Eastbourne: The last few minutes in, through Hampden Park. Eastbourne station sits at the end of a short branch, so trains carrying on to Hastings head back out the way they came.
about.Brighton|Lewes: Out through London Road, past the Amex Stadium at Falmer and under the South Downs to Lewes.
about.Hastings|Eastbourne: Along the coast through St Leonards and Bexhill, then across the Pevensey Levels, near where William the Conqueror landed in 1066.
about.Hastings|Polegate: Along the coast through St Leonards and Bexhill, then across the Pevensey Levels, near where William the Conqueror landed in 1066.
about.Ashford International|Rye: Across Romney Marsh on the Marshlink, single track for much of the way, with big skies and sheep on both sides.
about.Rye|Hastings: Through Winchelsea and the woods above Hastings, coming in through Ore.
about.Ashford International|Hastings: Across Romney Marsh on the Marshlink, through Rye and Winchelsea. It’s single track for much of the way, with big skies and sheep on both sides.
about.Portsmouth & Southsea|Havant: Off Portsea Island through Fratton and Hilsea.
about.Havant|Chichester: Along the edge of Chichester Harbour, through Emsworth and Bosham.
about.Chichester|Worthing: Through Barnham and Angmering, with the South Downs off to the north.
about.Worthing|Brighton: Along the coast through Lancing and Shoreham, past Shoreham Airport, so keep an eye out for light aircraft.
about.Havant|Brighton: The full West Coastway, through Chichester and Worthing and past Shoreham Airport.
about.Brighton|Haywards Heath: Up the main line through the Clayton tunnel under the South Downs.
about.East Croydon|Haywards Heath: Over the North Downs, through Gatwick and across the Ouse Valley Viaduct.
